text.p: Atlantic Pharmaceuticals Inc said it eradicated the deadly respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in 95 percent of infected tissue cultures using its 2-5A antisense technology.
The 2-5A antisense technology works by selectively binding to genetic material and blocking the production of proteins that cause the disease.
The company said it will probably be another two or three years before it completes preclinical toxicology studies and can proceed to human clinical trials.
However, it said it was excited by the early stage research since there is currently no approved vaccine or "highly effective" therapy for RSV.
Results of the study are published in the March issue of the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

RSV is the leading cause of lower respiratory infections such as pneumonia and brochiolitis in infants and children and is the cause of at least 90,000 hospitalizations and 4,500 deaths in the U.S. each year, Atlantic said.

The disease, which initially manifests itself with symptoms similar to those of the common cold such as runny nose, cough and fever, is most common in infants and children, but also attacks adults with compromised immune systems.
